name: WebAuthn sign in (get) and conditional mediation
plain: Signs the person in with a passkey, including autofill style suggestions.
meaning: Proves who the person is without a password. Conditional UI shows passkeys in the username field.

access.prompt_ui: Passkey sheet or autofill suggestion in the username field
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Signs the person in with a passkey, including autofill style suggestions.

limits.headline: Can sign you in with a passkey, even from the username box suggestions
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with a passkey, or pick one from the username box
can: Ask your device to prove you hold the passkey for that site
Show your passkeys as suggestions in the username box
Sign you in without you typing a password
cannot: Get your fingerprint, face or private key
Sign you in without your confirmation
Show username box suggestions in browsers too old to support them
limits.differs: Passkey sign in works in current Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox. The username box suggestions are newer and not in every browser.

story.what_it_is: Signs you in with a passkey, even offering it in the username box.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Apple pitches signing in by looking at your phone or touching a sensor, with no password to type.

marketing.name: Passkey autofill
marketing.pitch: Google describes passkeys that show up in the username field like saved passwords, so sign in is one tap.

story.for_you: You tap the username box and your account appears in the suggestions. You tap it and confirm with your face, fingerprint or PIN. You are in without typing a thing.
story.for_makers: Makers see higher sign in success and fewer help tickets. Because the passkey only works on the real domain, phishing fails, which protects both the user and the brand.

use_cases.example: A player opens a game account page and signs in with a tap in the username box before a big tournament sign up closes.
A cloud gaming site lets a person sign in on a smart TV browser by approving a passkey on a phone, then streams a game.
A bank website offers the passkey in the login field, so a customer logs in with Touch ID.
A shopper signs in at checkout with the passkey suggestion, finishing before the cart expires.
A team member opens an online editor and logs in with a passkey from their phone or laptop.
A fraud team treats a passkey sign in as a strong sign that the right person is present and loosens extra checks.

technical_bounds: Challenge must come from server; replay blocked
Conditional mediation is silent until the user picks
No cross site use without rpId related origin

abuse: Username enumeration if the site is sloppy

history.change: Hybrid transport by phone QR code
